Four competitors filed federal lobbying disclosures on telehealth topics in May 2026, signaling industry mobilization around access and economics policy at the state level. New York remains a top enforcement jurisdiction for medical advertising and anti-kickback compliance, particularly as telehealth utilization continues to drive state scrutiny of provider-marketplace relationships. The regulatory affairs lead should assess whether competitor positioning on federal policy creates downstream state-level rulemaking risk that affects marketplace advertising practices or provider credential verification standards.
